newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee called to open 3.00 to 4.00 lower.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee called to open 3.00 to 4.00 lower.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures were called to open 3.00 to 4.00 cents lower Tuesday as traders anticipate a technical correction to Monday's rally to near six-week highs.

Some traders, however, expected the market to come in closer to unchanged. "I'm looking for a corrective dip, but not that much," said one dealer. "We'll see some profit taking this morning, but I'm calling it flat to slightly lower."
New York arabica futures shot up Monday amid concerns of a shortage of exchange-certified coffee for delivery against the September contract.

CSCE September settled up 12.05 cents at 188.35 cents a lb after ranging from 189.50 to 178.00. Second-month December ended 7.15 cents higher at 164.40 cents, while the back months closed up 1.00 to 6.00.
The September/December switch, a barometer of near-term availability, bulged to 23.95 cents compared with 19.05 cents at the close on Friday.

After Monday's close, CSCE reported certified coffee stocks fell 750 60-kg bags as of July 25, to 92,078 bags -- or the equivalent of about 328 lots. An additional 2,367 bags were pending grading, the exchange said.
Technically, traders said September support was seen near 184.00-184.50 cents. On the upside, resistance was pegged at 190.70 cents, then 193.00-194.00 cents.

On the weather front, forecaster Weather Services Corp said on Tuesday that there is no damaging cold weather expected during the next seven days in Brazil's coffee belt, with low temperatures in the 50s to low 60s F (low to middle teens C).
London coffee futures were broadly higher early Tuesday, but off peaks. At the midday break, September was up $40, to $1,655, after ranging from $1,668 to $1,655. November also rose $40, to $1,645.
